seo_description: Psychological horror game where audio is the core gameplay mechanic. Built with Wwise, Unreal Engine 5, and C++.
hero.title: Shadow Frames
hero.subtitle: Audio Is the Only Weapon
concept.hook: Horror game where sound is the only weapon. No HUD, no markers. Just your ears.
concept.p1: Shadow Frames is set in a 1960s Irish pub, rendered entirely in black and white. Anomalies spawn every 30 to 50 seconds. Glasses levitate. Shadows drift on their own. Chairs spin. Audio is how you find them.
concept.p2: Mute the game and you're blind. Every creak, whisper, and rattle carries directional information that points you toward the next anomaly. Photograph it, pin it to the board, piece the story together. Sound isn't atmosphere here. It's the gameplay mechanic.
systems.footstep.title: Footstep Detection
systems.footstep.desc: A physics line-trace fires downward from the player's feet each step. The hit result's Physical Material maps to a Wwise Switch: wood, tiles, concrete, creaky wood. New surfaces get added in the editor without touching code.
systems.proximity.title: Enemy Proximity
systems.proximity.desc: Dual-threshold hysteresis state machine (start at 70%, stop at 60%) keeps the audio from flickering when the enemy hovers near a boundary. RTPC smoothly scales dread ambience and stress breathing as distance changes.
systems.anomaly.title: Anomaly System
systems.anomaly.desc: Three stages: alert burst on spawn, directional hint for location, then a sustained presence loop until you capture it. RTPC tension scaling drives intensity. Spatial audio cues are the only way to find anomalies. No UI markers exist.
gallery.title: Wwise Architecture
gallery.desc: Screenshots from the Wwise project showing the mixer hierarchy, DataAsset configurations, RTPC curves, and event structure.
code.title: Technical Deep Dive
code.hint: 3 annotated C++ snippets. Click lines with dots for explanations
challenge1.title: Audio Flickering at Proximity Boundaries
challenge1.hard: When the enemy hovered near the proximity trigger boundary, dread audio toggled on and off every frame. Players heard a machine-gun stutter instead of smooth tension. Terrible.
challenge1.did: I built a hysteresis state machine with separate start (70%) and stop (60%) thresholds. That 10% gap kills the boundary flickering entirely. RTPC handles smooth intensity transitions between thresholds.
challenge2.title: Surface Detection Without Per-Level Setup
challenge2.hard: The pub has 4 floor materials (wood, tiles, concrete, creaky wood). Manually tagging surfaces per level was slow and broke every time the level designer changed geometry. Nobody wanted to maintain it.
challenge2.did: Switched to Unreal's Physical Material system with line traces. Each physics material maps automatically to a Wwise Switch. Designers add new surfaces in the editor. No code changes, no per-level tagging.
